verses.text: After giving his twelve disciples these instructions, Jesus left to teach and preach in their towns.
When John heard in prison what the Messiah was doing, he sent two of his disciples
to ask him, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we expect someone else?”
Jesus answered them, “Go back and tell John what you hear and see:
the blind see, the lame walk, people with skin diseases are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear the Good News.
Blessed is anyone who doesn’t turn away because of me.”
As John’s disciples were leaving, Jesus began speaking to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed swaying in the wind?
What did you go out to see? Someone dressed in fancy clothes? People in fancy clothes live in kings’ palaces.
Then why did you go? To see a prophet? Yes—and I’m telling you, he’s more than a prophet.
He’s the one Scripture speaks about: ‘Look, I’m sending my messenger ahead of you. He will prepare your way before you.’
I’m telling you the truth: no one born of a woman has been greater than John the Baptist. Yet the least person in the Kingdom of Heaven is greater than he is.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, the Kingdom of Heaven has been treated violently, and violent people are trying to seize it.
All the Prophets and the Law spoke about what would happen up until John.
If you’re willing to accept it, John is the Elijah who was going to come.
Anyone with ears should listen.
“What can I compare this generation to? They’re like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling to their friends:
‘We played the flute for you, but you didn’t dance. We sang a funeral song, but you didn’t grieve.’
John came neither eating nor drinking, and people say, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and people say, ‘Look at him—a glutton and a drunk, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is shown to be right by what it produces.”
Then Jesus began condemning the towns where most of his miracles had happened, because they hadn’t turned back to God.
“How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the miracles done in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned back long ago, wearing sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell you, Tyre and Sidon will have an easier time on judgment day than you will.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you’ll be brought down to Hades. If the miracles done in you had happened in Sodom, it would still be standing today.
But I tell you, Sodom will have an easier time on judgment day than you will.”
At that time Jesus said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you’ve hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children.
Yes, Father, because this was pleasing to you.
“My Father has entrusted everything to me. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to reveal him to.
“Come to me, all of you who work hard and carry heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke and learn from me, because I’m gentle and humble in heart. You’ll find rest for your souls.
My yoke is easy to carry, and my burden is light.”
